parts.label: (a)
parts.text: Identify two characteristics of bipolar disorder.

parts.label: (b)
parts.text:
Describe rational emotive behaviour therapy (REBT) as a treatment for depression (Ellis,
1962).

parts.label: (c)
parts.text:
Explain one similarity and one difference between REBT and one biological treatment for
depression.

parts.label: (a)
parts.text: Describe explanations of phobias.

parts.label: (b)
parts.text:
Evaluate explanations of phobias, including a discussion of nature versus nurture. 
Psychology and consumer behaviour

parts.label: (a)
parts.text:
Lauterborn proposed ‘the 4 Cs marketing mix model’ of advertising.
Identify two of the ‘Cs’.

parts.label: (b)
parts.text:
Describe the procedure and one result from the study by Auty and Lewis (2004) on product
placement in films.

parts.label: (c)
parts.text: Explain one strength and one weakness of the study by Auty and Lewis.

parts.label: (a)
parts.text: Describe what psychologists have discovered about sound and consumer behaviour.

parts.label: (b)
parts.text:
Evaluate what psychologists have discovered about sound and consumer behaviour,
including a discussion about experiments. 
Psychology and health

parts.label: (a)
parts.text:
Explain why people with Type A personality are more likely to experience stress-related
illness.

parts.label: (b)
parts.text:
Describe stress inoculation training (SIT) as a technique for preventing stress (Meichenbaum,
1985).

parts.label: (c)
parts.text:
Explain one strength and one weakness of stress inoculation training (SIT) as a technique for
preventing stress.

Evaluate what psychologists have discovered about managing and controlling pain, including

parts.text: Explain what is meant by ‘enrichment’ as a job design technique.

parts.text: Describe the study on workplace sabotage by Giacalone and Rosenfeld (1987).

parts.label: (c)
parts.text: Explain two weaknesses of the study by Giacalone and Rosenfeld.
